# Judges Chapter 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_pages_288-289.jpg

1. And it was in those days, and there was no king in Yisrael. And there was a man, a Levite, sojourning in the remote parts of the hill-country of Ephrayim. And he took for himself a woman, a concubine, from Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah.

2. And his concubine played the harlot against him, and she went from him to the house of her father, to Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah. And she was there for a period of four months.

3. And her husband arose and went after her to speak upon her heart, to bring her back. And his servant [was] with him and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him into the house of her father. And the father of the young woman saw him and rejoiced to meet him.

4. And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, held him, and he dwelt with him three days. And they ate and drank and spent the night there.

5. And it was on the fourth day, and they rose early in the morning, and he arose to go. And the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "Sustain your heart [with] a morsel of bread, and afterward you shall go."

6. And the two of them sat and ate together and drank. And the father of the young woman said to the man, "Be willing, please, and spend the night, and let your heart be good."

7. And the man arose to go, and his father-in-law urged him, and he turned back and spent the night there.

8. And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go, and the father of the young woman said, "Please, sustain your heart." And they lingered until the declining of the day, and the two of them ate.

9. And the man arose to go — he and his concubine and his servant. And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, "Behold, please, the day has sunk toward evening. Please spend the night. Behold, the day is declining. Spend the night here, and let your heart be good, and you shall rise early tomorrow for your way, and you shall go to your tent."

10. And the man was not willing to spend the night. And he arose and went and came opposite Y'vus — she [is] Y'rushalayim — and with him [were] a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine [was] with him.

11. They [were] near Y'vus, and the day had gone down greatly. And the servant said to his master, "Come, please, and let us turn aside to this city of the Y'vusi and spend the night in it."

12. And his master said to him, "We will not turn aside to a city of foreigners, who [are] not of the sons of Yisrael. And we will pass on to Giv'ah."

13. And he said to his servant, "Come and let us draw near to one of the places, and we will spend the night in Giv'ah or in Ramah."

14. And they passed on and went, and the sun set upon them near Giv'ah, which [belongs] to Binyamin.

15. And they turned aside there to go in to spend the night in Giv'ah. And he went in and sat in the open square of the city, and there was no man gathering them into the house to spend the night.

16. And behold, an old man was coming from his work from the field in the evening. And the man [was] from the hill-country of Ephrayim, and he was sojourning in Giv'ah. And the men of the place [were] sons of Binyamin.

17. And he lifted his eyes and saw the traveling man in the open square of the city. And the old man said, "Where are you going, and from where do you come?"

18. And he said to him, "We [are] passing from Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah to the remote parts of the hill-country of Ephrayim. I [am] from there, and I went to Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah, and to the house of YHWH I am going, and there is no man gathering me into the house.

19. And also straw and also fodder there is for our donkeys, and also bread and also wine there is for me and for your maidservant and for the young man [who is] with your servants. There is no lack of any thing."

20. And the old man said, "Peace to you. Only, all your lack [is] upon me. Only, in the open square you shall not spend the night."

21. And he brought him into his house and mixed [feed] for the donkeys. And they washed their feet and ate and drank.

22. They [were] making their hearts good, and behold, the men of the city, men of the sons of B'liyya'al, surrounded the house, beating upon the door. And they said to the old man, the master of the house, saying, "Bring out the man who came into your house, and let us know him."

23. And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, "No, my brothers, do not do evil, please. After this man has come into my house, do not do this disgraceful thing.

24. Behold, my virgin daughter and his concubine — let me bring them out, please. And humble them and do to them the good in your eyes. And to this man, do not do the thing of this disgraceful deed."

25. And the men were not willing to listen to him. And the man seized his concubine and brought [her] out to them outside. And they knew her and abused her all the night until the morning. And they sent her away at the rising of the dawn.

26. And the woman came at the turning of the morning, and she fell at the entrance of the house of the man where her master [was], until the light.

27. And her master arose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way. And behold, the woman, his concubine, [was] fallen at the entrance of the house, and her hands [were] upon the threshold.

28. And he said to her, "Arise, and let us go." And there was no one answering. And he took her upon the donkey, and the man arose and went to his place.

29. And he came to his house and took the knife. And he seized his concubine and cut her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces. And he sent her throughout all the territory of Yisrael.

30. And it was, all who saw [it] said, "There has not been [such a thing] and there has not been seen [such a thing] from the day the sons of Yisrael came up from the land of Mitsrayim until this day. Set [your hearts] upon it, take counsel, and speak."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.2 — vattizneh alav ("she played the harlot against him"):** The MT reads zanah (to commit harlotry/fornication) with the preposition alav ("against him"). The LXX reads orgisthe auto ("she became angry with him") — a completely different scenario. The Vulgate follows the MT. The Old Latin has "she departed from him." The textual variant is significant: MT implies sexual infidelity as cause; LXX implies emotional conflict. Some scholars propose an original Hebrew verb za'am (to be angry) was corrupted to zanah. EMET follows the Leningrad Codex reading.

2. **v.18 — "to the house of YHWH I am going":** The MT reads beit YHWH (house of YHWH). Some manuscripts and versions read beiti (my house) — "I am going to my house." The LXX reads eis ton oikon mou ("to my house"). The difference is a single letter: yod vs. yod-he-vav. The Leningrad Codex reads YHWH, suggesting the Levite intended to go to a sanctuary.

3. **v.22 — "men of the sons of B'liyya'al":** b'nei b'liyya'al — literally "sons of worthlessness/destruction." The same phrase describes the wicked sons of Eli (1 Sam 2:12). Here the scene mirrors Genesis 19 (Sodom): strangers, hospitality, demand to "know" (yada') the male guest.

4. **v.25 — "the man seized his concubine":** vayachazek ba'ish b'pilagsho — the subject is the man (the Levite), not the old host. The Levite himself pushes his concubine out to the mob. The verb chazak (to seize, be strong) conveys force.

5. **v.29 — "cut her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces":** vay'natcheha la'atsameyha — literally "he cut her to her bones" (i.e., according to her limbs/joints). Twelve pieces for twelve tribes — a summons to war. The same act is performed by Saul with oxen in 1 Samuel 11:7, but there with animal flesh, not human.

— EMET, AI Translator
